sources.title: Grand Theft Auto VI launches tomorrow, November 19
sources.text: The latest installment in the Grand Theft Auto series heads to the state of Leonida, home to the neon-soaked streets of Vice City and beyond. Jason and Lucia have always known the deck is stacked against them. But when an easy score goes wrong, they find themselves on the darkest side of the sunniest place in America, in the middle of a criminal conspiracy stretching across the state of Leonida — forced to rely on each other more than ever if they want to make it out alive. Grand Theft Auto VI arrives on PlayStation 5 Thursday, November 19, available at PlayStation Store. The game is set in the state of Leonida, home to the neon-soaked streets of Vice City and beyond in the biggest, most immersive evolution of the series yet. Jason grew up around grifters and crooks. After a stint in the Army trying to shake off his troubled teens, he found himself in the Keys doing what he knows best, working for local drug runners. Meeting Lucia could be the best or worst thing to ever happen to him. Jason knows how he’d like it to turn out but right now, it’s hard to tell. Lucia’s father taught her to fight as soon as she could walk, and life has been coming at her swinging ever since. Fighting for her family landed her in the Leonida Penitentiary. Sheer luck got her out but now more than anything, Lucia wants the good life her mom has dreamed of since their days in Liberty City. Instead of half-baked fantasies, Lucia is prepared to take matters into her own hands. Leonida is made up of six regions: Vice City, the Leonida Keys, Grassrivers, Port Gellhorn, Ambrosia, and Mount Kalaga. Here’s a closer look at what makes each region unique. The glamour, hustle, and greed of America captured in a single city. Each neighborhood has something to offer, from the pastel art deco hotels and bright white sands of Ocean Beach, to the bustling panaderías of Little Cuba and the bootleg brands of the Tisha-Wocka flea market, out to the VC Port, the cruise ship capital of the world. We’re a long way from the ’80s, but Vice City is still the sun and fun capital of America Life in this tropical archipelago isn’t flashy but it’s easy. Get your buzz on and pull up a deck chair but look out — you are right on the doorstep of some of the most beautiful and dangerous waters in all of America. You never know what lies beneath the surface of this primordial expanse. The gators may be the most famous attraction, but there are far deadlier predators and weirder discoveries among the mangroves. Cheap motels, shut-down attractions, and empty strip malls won’t bring the tourists back, but there’s a new economy in this once-popular vacation spot. It’s fueled by malt liquor, painkillers, and truck stop energy drinks. In the heart of Leonida, American industry and old school values still reign supreme — whatever the cost. The Allied Crystal sugar refinery provides the jobs, while the local biker gang provides almost everything else. A national landmark up against the state’s northern border, Mount Kalaga offers prime hunting, fishing, and off-road trails. In the lush surrounding backwoods, hillbilly mystics and paranoid radicals live far from the prying eyes of the government. Spanning stations including Classic Rock, Modern Hip-Hop, Pop, Metal, Dance, Latin, ‘80s, Electronic, Blues, Ballads, Talk Radio, and much more, Grand Theft Auto VI features the biggest and widest-ranging selection of in-game radio yet. Plus, for the first time ever, Grand Theft Auto VI introduces a series of on-demand podcasts for Jason and Lucia to experience beyond Leonida’s terrestrial radio, with both radio and podcasts available to listen to in vehicles and on foot through newly introduced headphones and earbuds connected to their smartphones.

sources.text: O mais novo título da série Grand Theft Auto nos leva ao estado de Leonida, até as ruas iluminadas de neon de Vice City e além. Jason e Lucia sempre souberam que as cartas não estavam a favor deles. Mas quando o que deveria ser um trabalho fácil dá errado, eles se encontram no lado mais escuro do lugar mais ensolarado da América, no meio de uma conspiração criminosa que cobre todo o estado de Leonida, forçados a depender um do outro mais do que nunca se quiserem sair vivos. Grand Theft Auto VI chega para PlayStation 5 quinta-feira, 19 de novembro, disponível na PlayStation Store. O jogo se passa no estado de Leonida, onde ficam as ruas banhadas de neon de Vice City e além, na maior e mais imersiva evolução da série até hoje. Jason cresceu rodeado de bandidos e vigaristas. Após um período no exército para tentar se livrar de sua adolescência perturbada, ele se encontra nos Keys fazendo o que faz melhor, trabalhando para traficantes de drogas locais. Conhecer Lucia pode ser a melhor ou a pior coisa que já aconteceu com ele. Jason sabe como gostaria que tudo terminasse, mas agora, é difícil prever. O pai de Lucia a ensinou a lutar desde que ela aprendeu a andar, e a vida tem vindo com tudo para cima dela desde então. Lutar por sua família a colocou na Penitenciária de Leonida. Sorte pura a livrou desta vez, mas agora mais do que qualquer coisa, Lucia deseja a vida boa com a qual sua mãe sonhava desde que moravam em Liberty City. Em vez de fantasias pela metade, Lucia está preparada para assumir o controle da situação. Leonida é composto de seis regiões: Vice City, as Leonida Keys, Grassrivers, Port Gellhorn, Ambrosia, e Mount Kalaga. Vamos conhecer o que torna cada região única. O glamour, o trabalho e a ganância da América capturados em uma única cidade. Cada bairro tem algo a oferecer, dos hóteis de art deco, cores pastel e areia branca de Ocean Beach, até as padarias de Little Cuba e as marcas falsificadas do mercadinho de Tisha-Wocka, até o VC Port, a capital mundial dos navios de cruzeiro. Estamos longe dos anos 80, mas Vice City ainda é a capital do sol e da diversão da América. A vida neste arquipélago tropical não é chamativa, mas é boa. Pegue uma cervejinha e puxe uma cadeira de praia, mas tome cuidado, você está à beira das águas mais belas e perigosas da América. Você nunca sabe o que está sob a superfície desta região primordial. Os jacarés podem ser a atração mais famosa, mas há predadores bem mais perigosos e descobertas mais estranhas entre o manguezal. Motéis baratos, atrações fechadas, e galerias de lojas vazias e abandonadas não vão trazer os turistas de volta, mas há uma nova economia neste local que já foi um ponto turístico. Agora mandam o as bebidas baratas, remédios contra a dor e bebidas energéticas. No coração de Leonida, a indústria Americana e os antigos valores ainda reinam supremos, seja qual for o custo. A refinaria de açúcar Allied Crystal providencia os empregos, e a gangue de motociclistas local providencia quase todo o resto. Um marco nacional na fronteira norte do estado, Mount Kalaga oferece as melhores trilhas off-road e pontos de pesca e caça. Nas florestas em torno, caipiras místicos e radicais paranóicos vivem longe dos olhos vigilantes do governo. Com estações de Rock Clássico, Hip-Hop Moderno, Pop, Metal, Dance, Latina, Anos 80, Electrônica, Blues, Baladas, Talk Radio, e muito mais, Grand Theft Auto VI possui a maior e mais variada seleção de rádios em um jogo até hoje. Além disso, pela primeira vez, Grand Theft Auto VI apresenta uma série de podcasts sob demanda para Jason e Lucia ouvirem além das rádios de Leonida, com ambos disponíveis para ouvir em veículos e a pé usando fones de ouvido e earbuds conectados aos seus smartphones.

sources.text: Critics praise the "richly drawn and compelling romance" of Jason and Lucia in GTA 6, delivering a record Metacritic score After a 13-year wait, Grand Theft Auto 6 has been met with universal acclaim. Despite a lead-up marred by delays and leaks the hype has only grown, with over 17 million pre-orders generating more than $1.6 billion in revenue, according to recent data . Critics have spent weeks exploring Rockstar's Leonida, featuring the Bonnie-and-Clyde-inspired duo Jason and Lucia, leading to a Metacritic score of 99 . Backed by over 100 reviews, the title is currently listed as the platform's best game of all time , above the original N64 release of The Legend of Zelda: The Ocarina of Time. In the words of The Guardian 's Keza MacDonald: "Rockstar has created the most extraordinarily, indulgently detailed virtual world that we have seen yet." "Leonida is so lifelike that at times it beggars belief, so vast that it feels overwhelming [...] and contains so many potential experiences that it's hard to know where to start." IGN 's Luke Reilly emphasised that the wait for GTA 6 was reflected in the detail Rockstar has poured into its world. "This is a world that feels more lived-in and real than anything I've ever played, and it's one you can interact with at a level never seen before in the series," he said. "Rockstar has truly pushed the boat out.” The game's level of detail raised concerns about performance, particularly its 30fps cap on all consoles , including the PlayStation 5 Pro. However, Reilly found that this limitation did not diminish the experience. "What matters to me is that it looks absolutely incredible and runs smoothly and reliably on a standard PS5. I find all the brilliant visual flourishes far more important, from the concentric rings of ripples on water due to helicopter rotor downwash, to the almost imperceptible line of sweat that appears on Lucia's forehead after a brisk jog, or the buckling of the fabric on a shirt as torsos twist, to the temporary dents on a punching bag as you strike it." "If a sufficiently stable and properly paced 30fps is the route to GTA 6 looking and functioning the way it does, bug-free, then I have no complaints." GTA 6's immersion extends to daily routines that improve stats like health and stamina, or managing car fuel levels. As Game Informer 's Matt Miller observed, these activities "add pacing and counterpoint to the explosive march of major missions, narrative threads, and set-piece encounters that drive the game forward." These everyday moments are initially character-specific, as The New York Times' Yussef Cole noted. "Jason can opt to fix up his run-down bachelor pad in preparation for Lucia's imminent release. There are numerous tasks around the house, like putting up drywall, painting and fixing the roof, that take up the player's time and the character's in-game resources, but they aim toward a productive and satisfying goal: a better relationship." That's not to say GTA 6 isn't like past games, where violence is encouraged and chaos is one petty crime away. Miller emphasised that these moments do not detract from the "meticulously choreographed" set pieces, which "run the gamut from amusing shenanigans at a strip club to intense chases and escapes fueled by raging gunfights and explosions. Many of the best moments leverage an expert sense of musical accompaniment, weaving a slick original score alongside one of the most impressive and wide-ranging licensed soundtracks ever heard in a video game – often to surprisingly emotional effect." Critics agreed that GTA 6 offers unexpected emotional depth, thanks to nuance in both the representation of the lead characters and the player's ability to control them. IGN's Reilly described Jason and Lucia as "unlike any leads that have come before them in the series," whose priorities are each other and escaping the criminal life they find themselves increasingly entrenched in. "They're not angels, and it is invariably their recklessness as small-time crooks that puts them in the wrong place at the wrong time, but the overall sliminess of their far more powerful antagonists does make the couple easy to root for throughout their story,"he wrote. The New York Times' Cole agreed, adding that the emphasis on the duo's relationship "reflects a maturation of a series that has generally only told stories about men solipsistically chasing after their own success." He continued: "Choosing romance is the easy part, thanks to the chemistry and human characterisation of the two leads. Lucia and Jason's relationship builds on itself and becomes a constant, supportive presence. It gets reflected in the story missions too, as your characters make scripted choices that reflect how you behaved toward each other in the idle moments in between." Game Informer's Miller described Jason and Lucia's relationship as "elevating the game to new heights, lending this instalment a heart, tension, and emotional core missing from prior entries." "This is, without a doubt, video gaming's most richly drawn and compelling romance, featuring two leads who are immediately relatable and compelling to watch. Player actions dictate the strength of their bond, deepening the sense of engagement. Like the best crime fiction, you're left surprised by how much you cheer for two people who regularly commit terrible acts." The Guardian's MacDonald "found it impossible not to care" for the couple over time. "They are our avatars in GTA 6's world, but they are not blank stand-ins for the player: you decide their actions but not their personalities. They feel like real people rather than puppets dancing to your whim [...] When the story gave me opportunities to decide what would happen next, what came to mind for me was what they would do, not what I would do." sources.title: Cyberleek Returns for GTA 6 Launch to Reportedly Release a Near-Complete Xbox Build, Threatens to Release the Game's Executable in Days
sources.text: Cyberleek has returned for the launch of GTA 6 to allegedly release a near complete Xbox build of the game — and has threatened to release its executable in just days. It was thought that the person or group responsible for the online Cyberleek persona had ended their spate of GTA 6 leaks last month, after their memecoin crashed despite efforts to boost its market cap. In October, Cyberleek had tied various types of GTA 6 gameplay leaks to the Cyberleek market cap, and threatened to release a build of the game — supposedly over 200 GB in size — if the memecoin hit a $30 million market cap. Gameplay clips reportedly leaked at the time allegedly showed Lucia fully naked — something that is not possible in the final launch version of the game. Yesterday, November 19 — the GTA 6 release date — Cyberleek returned to drop a GTA 6 Xbox build without the game's executable. In a statement reportedly published online , Cyberleek claimed this Xbox build is a “full November 2026 build of GTA 6.” They predicted this Xbox build would be used to emulate GTA 6 on PC “within a week, running far past 30fps.” The console version of GTA 6 targets 30fps across all platforms, although struggles at times to hit that on base PS5 and Xbox Series X and S. Cyberleek has revived their crypto scheme, promising to release the executable immediately if it hits a $15 million market cap. While the CyberLeek memecoin was boosted in value by the news to $1.9 million yesterday, it is unlikely to get anywhere near the target. Still, Cyberleek has vowed to release the final file anyway on November 23, whether the memecoin hits the market cap or not. The release of a full and recent build of GTA 6 would of course be hugely damaging for Rockstar and parent company Take-Two, which appears to have been unable to deter Cyberleek’s actions in any meaningful way since their spate of leaks began. It would also run counter to the thought that Cyberleek only had access to an early development build of GTA 6, a feeling that was reinforced not only by the videos that were released, but by the differences that have emerged following the game’s official launch. Fans are calling on people not to spend money on Cyberleek, pointing out the leaker cashed out back in August and did again in October. Analysis of cryptocurrency transactions in late August pointed to the GTA 6 leaker cashing out having earnt around $270,000. IGN had reported on fan skepticism around the alleged leaked gameplay that reportedly showed both Jason and Lucia fully naked . A previous leaked gameplay video allegedly showed a tank spawning into the world, which suggested access to a dev menu of some kind. The leaked videos allegedly showing both Jason and Lucia fully naked also show NPCs failing to react to that in any way, which suggested this effect was achieved with either a dev menu or cheats. Cyberleek had threatened Rockstar and Take-Two with the release of a full playthrough of the game’s story if they failed to release GTA 6 on-disc and issue a public apology — and the market cap of the memecoin hit $30 million. Of course, few believe these GTA 6 leaks are about campaigning for physical media — rather they're about making money from a crypto scam. Cyberleek appeared to go dark after a spate of high-profile GTA 6 leaks in August that sparked an investigation from Take-Two. The company issued subpoenas to the likes of Discord as part of the hunt for the person or group of people responsible. It remains unclear how the gameplay footage, or any potential build of the game it's taken from, escaped the confines of Rockstar's infamous tight security. In August, Rockstar addressed the GTA 6 leaks , describing the situation as "heartbreaking" for its development team and "unfortunate" for fans. At the time, the developer acknowledged that its intended experience for players "may now be impacted by some spoilers," but reiterated GTA 6's previously-confirmed launch date of November 19. Whether the culprit or culprits are ever caught may rest on how successful Take-Two's legal team and the relevant authorities are at forcing social networks or crypto exchanges to divulge any personal details they hold on those responsible. sources.title: How to Get Ready for November 19
sources.text: November 19, 2026, has long been circled on your calendar. Birthdays, anniversaries, and holidays have come and gone, but this day belongs to you and your XBOX console. We can hardly believe it’s almost here, either. Once midnight strikes, you want to be locked in the action, so to help you prepare, we created a checklist to ensure distractions are put to bed so you can settle in for a season of gaming like nothing you’ve ever experienced before. 2026 has been full of some absolute bangers: Gears of War E-Day, Call of Duty: Modern Warfare 4, Forza Horizon 6, Halo: Campaign Evolved, Minecraft Dungeons II, Diablo 4: Lord of Hatred , Control Resonant , Mixtape , Pragmata , The Blood of Dawnwalker , Star Wars: Galactic Racer , 007 First Light , Ace Combat 8: Wings of Theve … seriously, all these games came out this year . That also means you might have a hard drive that is nearing capacity. And you will be faced with some hard choices to free up approximately 212GB of space on your XBOX Series X|S before November 19. You could always upgrade the capacity of your console to keep all your games at the ready, using the storage expansion slot on the back of the console. Otherwise, you’ll have a hard choice to make which we do not envy. But know that you’re in good company – we had to find a way to make room too. XBOX Cloud Gaming means that you don’t need to own an XBOX Series X|S console to experience the latest games (or use up that hard drive space) – you can stream directly from the cloud to your XBOX One console. Game Pass subscribers receive an allotment of hours per month as part of their plans, but you can also purchase blocks of time . Certain upcoming major releases have been confirmed as cloud-ready on day one , so even if you don’t own a current gen console, your latest obsession isn’t out of reach. You never want to settle in for a long gaming session only to immediately get hit with an update download. If you haven’t used your XBOX Series X|S or XBOX One in a minute, be sure to power up and connect to the internet beforehand and make sure you’re all set with the latest system updates. You can also install any upcoming releases you may have pre-ordered, while you’re at it. If you’re feeling a gaming flu coming on (and there’s a lot of that going around right now), then take a sick day, rather than risk infecting your coworkers or classmates. Sometimes you just need to listen to your body’s needs, relax, and let the fever run its course. Miami’s own DJ Khaled, aka Dr. XBOX will write you a personalized note to help explain the situation. If this thing is really serious, you may even need the whole week to recover – it’s the responsible thing to do. We all have responsibilities. Some of them come with four legs and a suspect bladder. Don’t let Rufus ruin your gaming fun. Get ahold of a local dog walker to take them outside so you can enjoy the big day uninterrupted. Or drop them off at doggie daycare for a day (or week) to get them out of your hair. Is your XBOX in an area of the house that is easily accessible to younger players? Consider the steps you need to take to get it out of younger sightlines, like running an extension cable out to the shed in the backyard or huddling up in your at-home office. Even if you do find yourself bouncing between rooms, your save files reside in the Cloud, allowing you to pick up your session wherever you last plugged your console in. We’re always on the hunt for new tunes and one of the things we’re most looking forward to on November 19 is discovering a whole bunch of new tracks that are sure to make our listening playlist pop throughout the year. You can get started here on Spotify . XBOX Design Lab lets you create your own next-gen XBOX Wireless Controller. Choose from a combination of colors, patterns, textured grips, and more. You could even pick up some specially themed versions of controllers styled in hot pink and pastels – this one is particularly striking . Speaking of controllers, if you expect long gaming sessions in your near future, make sure that it’s plugged in so it has a full charge when you need it, or stock up on AA batteries. Maybe even get a backup controller ready so you can hot-swap them in and minimize interruptions. Looking for something to add to your queue? Check out the 1967 classic, “Bonnie and Clyde,” featuring Warren Beatty and Faye Dunaway to get you in the mood for an epic story about two tragic lovers who fall into a life of crime. We’ll have to wait and see if the outcome is any different this time around starting on November 19.

I'm excited to see what other Easter eggs pop up as more players explore the depths of Vice City in GTA 6, honestly. The game has only just landed in players' hands, though – but something tells me it won't be too long before we see Easter egg roundups surface online. sources.text: Bigfoot stalks Jason in GTA 6… or does he? GTA 6 players have already encountered something that they are calling “Bigfoot”. The clip that has been widely circulating online of players running into Bigfoot, isn’t Bigfoot. It’s a character that the locals refer to as Skunkape. sources.title: Players Are Surprised at How Well the Xbox Series S Handles GTA 6
sources.text: In the run-up to GTA 6 's launch, one of the biggest questions players were pondering was how well the Xbox Series S would handle Rockstar's highly anticipated game. Now that it's out in the wild, Series S owners are celebrating the fact that it actually runs the game pretty well on the console. All of the marketing footage leading up to GTA 6's launch was running on either the PS5 or the PS5 Pro, both of which are much more powerful than the Xbox Series S. When gameplay was finally revealed in August running at 30fps on the PS5, people understandably got a bit nervous about the Xbox Series S. But, thanks to Microsoft and AMD porting FSR 4.1 to the Xbox Series S last month, the game runs surprisingly well. It's not hard to see why so many people love the Xbox Series S. It's far and away the most cost-effective method to get a current-generation console, even after this year's price increases shot the price up to $499 . Even at that cost, it's still cheaper than the Nintendo Switch 2, and Nintendo's handheld can't play GTA 6. Sabía que tarde o temprano la gente iba a ver el valor de la xbox series S https://t.co/bHdgBCqweK Unsurprisingly, now that the Series S can decently handle GTA 6 (albeit with some frame drops here and there), Series S owners have been celebrating. Over on X/Twitter, user Scavenger928 posted a photoshopped image of Michael Jordan hugging the Series S, with a caption that translates to, "I knew sooner or later people would see the value of the Xbox Series S." Over on Reddit, there are several posts in the Xbox Series S subs from players who are surprised at how well the game holds up on the little Xbox. User either-ambition-9846 posted their findings about the port, surprised at how well GTA 6 runs, capping it off by saying, "I think the main point I want people to take away if you’re concerned about how well it’s going to perform, you’ll get immersed into the storyline and gameplay, the little frame drops that you might notice at the start, will slowly fade away. It’s a beautiful game, just go and enjoy it and forget about the squabbling on here." In the comments to that post, one user, shoddyartichoke2365 was even surprised that running GTA 6 on the Xbox Series S didn't cause the poor thing to melt, saying, "It's not too noisy or hot, surprisingly just as warm as it is on other games." GTA 6 has been received extremely well across the board. It's already tied with The Legend of Zelda: Ocarina of Time for the best-reviewed game of all time. Here at IGN, we gave it a 10 out of 10, where reviewer Luke Reilly called it, "Exquisitely detailed, endlessly ripe for experimentation, and uncompromisingly engineered, Grand Theft Auto 6 is the single most impressive video game I have ever played." When I tested GTA 6 on the Xbox Series S in the wee hours of the morning yesterday, I was also surprised at how well the 1440p machine handled the game. I can still absolutey tell the difference between it and the Xbox Series X version, but the game plays well, despite dropping frames occasionally. And, if anything, the game running as well as it does on the Xbox Series S bodes well for the inevitable PC version – maybe playing it on a handheld gaming PC won't be totally out of the question. sources.text: What is the best way to make money in GTA 6? GTA 6 is finally here and players around the world are getting a chance to jump in to the world of Grand Theft Auto 6 after 13 years. However in GTA 6, money isn’t easy to get early in the game, and as such players have been looking for a way to make money fast in GTA 6. In this guide we’ll list the best ways to make money and GTA 6 from early game stick-ups which you can do almost from the start of the game, to later-game bank robberies which will yield the highest rewards but are also the most difficult. If you are enjoying GTA 6 you should check out our GTA 6 Guides Hub and make sure you bookmark it. We will be updating that hub every day for the forseble future with new guides new walkthroughs and everything you need to know about Grand Theft Auto 6. Guides: If you're playing Grand Theft Auto 6, make sure to checkÂ out ourÂ complete walkthrough hub , featuringÂ beginner tips , navigation experience explained , GTA 6 cheats , and more. Robbing groceries stores in Grand Theft Auto 6 is one of the fastest ways to make money though you might not make a lot of it. Every groceries store in the game can be robbed. You can do this by going up to the cashier and sticking them up with a weapon. To do this approach, the cashier and hold the L2 button. This will aim your gun at the cashier without firing however at this point you can now interact with the cashier and threaten them which will cause them to open the cash register. You won’t get a lot of cash doing it this way, however there is little police response when you rob groceries stores. Some grocery stores also have a safe in the back room or you can access by kicking down the door or forcing the employee to open it for you. If that safe has a code you can often find the code on a post-it note located near the safe, or you can threaten the employee and you will get an option to ask them about the safe code. Eventually the police will be contacted and they will turn up at the store but by that point you should be long gone. It’s also worth noting that a lot of grocery stores have secret rooms of that sometimes include gang activity. you can tell if one of the grocery stores has a secret room by checking the minimap if there is a room that you haven’t accessed yet try picking the lock off the door or going back outside and checking another entrance. When you first get the ability to sell drugs, you can start robbing gang hideouts which often contain large amounts ofÂ various drugs that sell for a lot of money. This is by far one of the best ways to make money in GTA 6. The type of drug that the gang hideout is hiding has a huge effect on what it is worth for example things like weed are fairly cheap, but things like crystal and cocaine are far more expensive. You will know you are near a gang hideout because when will drive past and a yellow icon will appear on your map. At this point it is worth checking out what is there and if you check on the map you can also see the valuables that are available and that gang hideout If you steal drugs from a gang hideout you will have to physically take them to somewhere that you can sell them. However, later in the game if you do a lot of drug selling, some buyers will allow you to drop the drugs and a garage. Keep in mind, however, they will arrange a pick up and this means they will take a bigger cut of the money. Robbing jewellery stores and pawn shops is also a great way to make money in GTA 6. Howeverm these jewelry stores and pawn shops often have a high level of security so you are going to want to do some reconnaissance before you attempt to rob them. A lot of jewelry shops can be accessed from the back of the shop, where you will also be able to disable their security systems or if they have CCTV camera footage,Â you can destroy it.Â Doing this will delay the response time of the police, which is important because stealing from jewelry shops or pawn shops gets you a higher wanted level than stealing from a grocery store. One of the best ways to make money and Grand Theft Auto 6 is by completing main story missions. Often these main story missions will give you a big chunk of cash, so it’s worth doing as many of them as you can. This also applies to side missions which often provide you with a lot of cash. Just remember to take it to the bank to put in your account or it could be a lost if you are arrested or die. If you don’t have a bank account yet, check out our guide to Buck Me.Â Another great way to make money in GTA 6 is to sell cars. You will gain the ability to sell cars to Moses when you reach chapter 2 of GTA 6. He will take cars that do not have a tracker on them. On average you will get between $1000 and $5,000 dollars per car that you sell to Moses. After you sell a car to Moses there is a cooldown period where you can no longer sell cars to him however if you sleep at the safe house this cooldown period will elapse. Later in the game you can sell higher value cars to another prominent side character that is introduced and a later chapter . The ultimate way to make money and Grand Theft Auto 6 is to rob a banks.Â You won’t be able to rob banks straight away, in fact you will have to wait until you get the dye pack jammer during a mission where you rob a bank with a prominent side character. After this, you can rob banks whenever you like and it is by far the easiest way to make a huge amount of money in the game. Bank robberies are split up into several sections. There are basic cash drawers which you can get by threatening the tellers, there are safe which hide large numbers of marked bills, and then there are the bank vaults which house the largest amounts of money and in the game. With that being said, because of the amount of money you can get from robbing a bank, actually robbing a bank is also one of the most difficult things to do in the game. sources.text: I guess that's why the cars have speedometers. While you can switch to first-person temporarily in Grand Theft Auto 6 when you want to get a real good close-up of a texture or when you're looking at your phone, you can't run around doing crimes and having fun like you could when GTA 5 got its first-person mode. Except actually you can, as discovered by players on Reddit and tested by our own Morgan Park. It's easy enough to activate in-game. Go to the controller settings, then under the Controller Features section change your touch pad/select button to Camera 2 / 2. Get into a car, bring up your phone with the D-pad, press Circle or B then quickly hit Select. There you go, first-person GTA 6. As Morgan's footage shows, it's completely playable. It doesn't look 100% done, however, with your shoulders clipping through the camera when you've got a longarm gun up. Seeing someone break into a car in first-person also looks a bit rough around the edges. While conspiracy theorists have convinced themselves that Rockstar is holding back this feature to sell it as DLC, I figure they're probably still polishing it to add in a future update. If you want to leave first-person, you'll have to reload a save. It doesn't have to be an old save, though. sources.title: Playing GTA 6 this weekend? Here's 16 spoiler-free tips for your first playthrough
sources.text: It's launch weekend for GTA 6 - in case you hadn't noticed - and since I've played the best part of a hundred hours of this thing, I thought it might be useful to share a few pieces of advice from my time with it. Many of these are most applicable for the early game, but there are a few that'll be worth bearing in mind throughout. After last night's driving around I would also maybe add in a quick bonus one, come to think of it: watch out for cyclists making last-minute left turns. Or don't, actually. Half of this lot deserve it… The below list is spoiler-free, so you can relax if you're anxious about going through the story entirely fresh. Though naturally I do explain the way some parts of this game work, taking away some of the sense of discovery. You can take my word for it that there's plenty more to discover beyond this though, so worry not. If you'd like even more help navigating Leonida, then check out our wonderful guide team's GTA 6 walkthrough . The number one thing I'd tell people to do in GTA 6 is to create lots of save files and, as you progress and start needing to overwrite them, to try to keep a roughly even spread of files through each chapter. There are various reasons for this - for one, while the game autosaves, it doesn't seem to do that successfully if you suddenly lose power to the console or witness a rare game crash, so it'll preserve your progress. More than that: GTA's story and missions are surprisingly, perhaps mysteriously reactive. Quite a lot can differ, and so being able to go back and make different choices, or play the game differently, will be something 'future you' likely appreciates. In the very early game you won't have access to a bank account, but once you do: you should put every bit of cash you have in there as soon as you can. Cash is lost on death or arrest - which can happen quite often in GTA 6, funnily enough - and there's no real benefit to carrying it around. Just about everything, besides in-game strippers, can be paid for via your BuckMe account directly. And there's a relatively low $20,000 limit you really don't want to hit in the middle of raiding a gang hideout, either. GTA 6 has a luxurious range of customisation settings, from hiding notifications about your relationship to reinstating the old 'tap to sprint' control scheme. The accessibility settings - while crucially I'm not an expert - seem considerable. And there are somewhat disguised difficult settings here around enemy damage taken and encounters with the police. Fairly early in the game you'll gain access to the Scooter Bros. App, which lets you repair or summon your owned vehicles at will. Crucially, there's also an option to pay a one-off fee to unlock three free uses of the app per day. At $12,000, in the early game this is a lot of dosh, but once you rack up that kind of money after advancing through the game a little, it's well worth the initial cost. The sooner you unlock it, the more value it provides over time on a cost-per-use basis. And trust me when I say: as the game's intensity ramps up, you will probably find yourself needing to repair and recover your vehicles quite often. (Also, in Chapter 1, before you get access to the app, you can access the same service by going to your phone's contacts and calling Joey - handy!) Rockstar has somewhat disincentivised it by adding a cost and putting it in your phone's apps rather than the main map screen, but you can fast travel around Leonida if you ever want or need to. This is done via the RideMe Uber-like app. It's not cheap - you'll need to pay both the fee for the journey and an additional $100 to skip that journey and instantly arrive at your destination, but in certain scenarios it might prove useful. To skip the journey, hold L2/LT once in the cab, and then hold down Triangle/Y when the option is shown. However… While it's possible to journey-skip your way around this world, having tested that first hand I'd advise against it. It might be obvious, but GTA 6 is genuinely designed around you manually travelling around, typically in the car. If you skip all your commutes between missions or locations, you'll miss out on the game's dozens and dozens of emergent events, which lead to anything from one-off jokes to entire mission chains. The car is also, in a way, kind of the heart of the entire game. Relish the intentional slowness! Again, avoiding spoilers here, but in the mid game the 'true' loop of GTA 6 gameplay will properly reveal itself, in all the many methods of earning money and the increased emphasis on doing so. You can of course play the game however you like, but having reached the end and looked back from that point, I found that if there was a particular moment to set aside as the time for aimlessly exploring the world, it was from around Chapter 3 onwards. You'll have enough tools to be able to see it at more or less its fullest then, but also won't have missed anything essential by waiting until that point to take your foot off the pedal either. A handy early-game tip here that even I missed when I was playing, but have since discovered: two islands in the small cluster of them to the south-west of Jason's early game home each house a really useful weapon, in a silenced pistol and a handy shotgun. You'll own these permanently once found, and so they can be incredibly helpful for navigating missions with maximum or minimal violence. Look for shipwrecks on those islands to find them. The pistol is hidden under a little hatch on the deck of a shipwreck on the southernmost point of the south-easternmost island. The shotgun is next to a small wooden wrecked boat around the middle of the northernmost island. A mechanic I slightly underused at first was the ability to 'save' a given outfit to your car. sources.title: Amazon Drops Lightning Deals on Some of the Best Modern Board Games for Black Friday
sources.text: You can never have too many board games. With video games and TV dominating our attention on a daily basis, there's nothing better than sitting down and having a physical experience with your family and friends. A good game of Monopoly or Scrabble is always entertaining, but if you're looking to upgrade to something a bit more modern, Black Friday sales are a great time to do so. Amazon just dropped a number of Lightning Deals on some of our favorite modern tabletop games in 2026. Amazon's Black Friday sale kicked off on November 19, so these board game deals are new to today. You can dive into our top picks right here or scroll down for some of IGN's reviews on these games. Seeing as these are Lightning Deals, we don't expext these discounts to last through the weekend. The majority of Amazon's new board game deals are from Asmodee. That's not too surprising considering they own a variety of different studios. While we haven't reviewed every board game on this list, we have played all of them and can attest to just how fun they are. If you're looking for new tabletop experiences, any of these options are an easy recommendation. You can check out some of our hands-on reviews with these games below if you want to know more about the experience. This is one of the best Lord of the Rings board games on the market right now. We gave it an 8 out of 10 score in our review : "Lord of the Rings: Fate of the Fellowship expands on the 2008's Pandemic game system and manages to create one of the best Lord of the Ring tabletop experiences out there, but its increased reliance on random card draws and dice rolls can lead to some turns feeling wasted, or that you are biding your time for what you need, detracting from the game's excitement." - Scott White If you're looking for a racing board game, look no further than this one right here. We gave this game a 9 out of 10 in our review : "Heat: Pedal to the Metal is a vivid and delightful racing board game that surpasses the accomplishments of all that came before it. It’s an inspired title in both product and design, offering a range of options while presenting a dynamic racing system that is extremely impressive." - Charlie Theel For a fun and unique family board game , Harmonies is an excellent choice. We gave it an 8 out of 10 in our review : "Harmonies masterfully blends its drafting system and token-laying mechanics to create a satisfying gameplay loop with just the right amount of tension in its decision-making. At its core, it's an elegant optimization puzzle that offers a fresh challenge every time you play. The added verticality introduces another layer of strategy as you work to build the perfect mix of habitats. Its playful, inviting design features vibrant colors and beautifully illustrated animal cards that are a joy to engage with throughout the game. It's quick to set up and easy to teach, making it a great fit for families and couples, while still offering enough crunchy decisions to keep seasoned players satisfied." - Matt Adler If you're looking for a fun strategy game with civilization elements, 7 Wonders will be right up your alley. It's not for everyone, but it's still worth picking up at this price. We gave it a 7 out of 10 in our review : "You can’t argue with the sheer number of copies that 7 Wonders has sold, nor the plethora of awards that it has accrued. This is a fun game, a good way to pass a half hour, with a great balance of luck and strategy. But it got that way by spreading itself quite thin, making a lot of gamers fairly happy rather than bringing ecstasy to smaller fanbases. There are times when the lack of theme and long-term strategy makes it feel more like an exercise than a game and it’s a tad too involved for casual family play. But whatever kind of games you like, if you fancy taking the plunge, you’re almost guaranteed to find plenty of enjoyment." - Matt Thrower Jacob Kienlen is a Senior Audience Development Strategist and Writer for IGN. sources.text: Rockstar co-founder issues rare public statement as the firm's latest release launches worldwide Rockstar Games president and co-founder Sam Houser has issued a rare statement as GTA 6 launches, celebrating the game's debut and its glowing critical reception . "Rockstar Games was founded on the belief that games could achieve the same distinction as all other forms of storytelling, become essential to modern culture, and to be thought of as stories and worlds that live on with all of us," said Houser in a statement shared with IGN . "This week, Grand Theft Auto returns to Leonida and modern-day Vice City. While things have changed and time has passed, one aspect holds true: We have tried to create an experience that will exceed your expectations while showing what this medium is capable of, and why we believe games are so special. "Whether you can trace your journey to this game through the entire series or are experiencing Grand Theft Auto for the first time, this is a narrative set in a world full of possibilities – and it is up to you as the player to shape how it ultimately feels, and concludes. "We hope it felt both familiar and entirely new, and above all, we hope that you had fun. We are incredibly grateful to you and everything that you do to celebrate games. We look forward to many more years of sharing these experiences with you. The game is currently available to players in New Zealand and Australia, and will unlock at midnight on the 19th in other territories. The review embargo lifted this morning, with the game receiving near-universal critical acclaim and setting record viewership figures on YouTube and Twitch .

The 8BitDo 64 was a loose remake of the Nintendo 64’s unusual triple-grip controller that did away with that gamepad’s centered analog stick. But with its new GC Bluetooth Gamepad , 8BitDo has done a much better job at staying faithful to the design of the Nintendo GameCube’s excellent controllers, including their unique button layout, thumbstick design, and shoulder buttons. The 8BitDo GC Bluetooth Gamepad is available for preorder starting today for $49.99 in orange or purple and is expected to start shipping on December 10th. That’s much cheaper than Nintendo’s $69.99 wireless remake of the GameCube controller, although 8BitDo’s version isn’t an exact copy of the original’s shape and ergonomics. If that’s important to you, and you have your GameCube’s original accessories on hand, you can still buy 8BitDo’s $25.98 upgrade kit, which is a cheaper way to make it compatible with modern consoles and devices. 8BitDo’s GameCube redux carries forward the original’s octagonal gates around the base of each thumbstick, making it well-suited to playing fighting games like Super Smash Bros. Ultimate . And while Nintendo continues to skip modern thumbstick technologies , the 8BitDo GC features both drift-resistant TMR thumbsticks and Hall effect linear triggers. The controller connects to all versions of the Nintendo Switch over Bluetooth, as well as PCs or handheld consoles running Windows. It also comes with a 2.4GHz wireless USB receiver for players who prefer a connection with lower latency, or you can connect it with a USB-C cable for the best possible performance.
